audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rates this 8.5/10 'Hard matchup' and gives Swain five of seven stages while simultaneously marking diff 'FAV'. The Emerald+ figure is 54.15% over 591 games in Malphite's favour, and the content layer's own whys[5] and whys[6] say Malphite out-trades from first item onward.
audit.why: Difficulty, the level chart and the win rate have to tell one story. Swain genuinely owns levels 1-3 — Death's Hand reaches 750 against Seismic Shard's 625 and its cooldown falls from 7s to 3s as he ranks it — but a 54% lane is not 8.5/10 hard, and the late stages are not his.
audit.corrected: Early lane is Swain's on range. From Levels 4-5 it evens and from first item Malphite is favoured, matching the 54.15% headline.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and wants.you[1] build the Malphite item spike around stacking armour (Bramble Vest, Sunfire) 'so his AP drain barely dents your Granite Shield buffer'.
audit.why: Every ability Swain owns is magic damage — Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, Nevermove, and the Demonic Ascension drain. Armour reduces none of it. Armour is still worth buying, but for the opposite reason: Ground Slam's damage is calculated from Malphite's Armor, so it is an offensive stat here, not a defensive one. The full layer already says 'Build MR (not armor)', so the two layers currently contradict each other on the single most consequential build decision in the matchup.
audit.corrected: MR is the defensive buy (Mercury's Treads, Spirit Visage line). Armour is an offensive buy because Ground Slam scales off it. Grievous Wounds matters because Ravenous Flock souls and the R drain are his sustain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (E: 'deals magic damage based on his Armor')

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings — spikes[2], wants.you[0], mid, late and whys[4] — claim Unstoppable Force knocks Swain up and 'interrupts his channeled R drain mid-cast' / 'cancels the drain and the soul stacks he lives on'.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is not a channel. Riot's text: 'Swain transforms into a demon and drains health from nearby enemy champions, minions, and neutral monsters. Swain can cast Demonflare... This form is indefinite as long as' the drain keeps feeding it. A transform is not interrupted by displacement, and the kit file carries no channel flag on the ability. This is the most dangerous line in the entry: it tells the player to spend a 130s ultimate expecting the fight to change, and it does not.
audit.corrected: Unstoppable Force displaces Swain and opens your burst, but it does not switch Demonic Ascension off. What starves the form is bodies — it drains nearby champions, minions and monsters — so fight him away from the wave and bring Grievous Wounds.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json (R Demonic Ascension description; no channel flag; cd 120)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is called an 'E hook-line' and an 'E pull into root' throughout, and nothing states how it actually roots.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The outgoing wave does not root — the return leg does. That is the entire dodge, and it is counter-intuitive: the ability looks like it missed, and the player who relaxes once it has passed gets rooted from behind. Calling it a hook teaches precisely the wrong reaction. 850 range, 12s at rank 1 falling to 10s, and shorter while Demonic Ascension is active.
audit.corrected: Nevermove roots on the return leg, not the outgoing one — step sideways after the wave has passed you, not before it arrives.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard appears only as a slow ('Use Q Seismic Shard's slow to dodge his E hook-line'). Nothing says it steals Move Speed.
audit.why: It transfers speed for 3 seconds — Malphite gains exactly what Swain loses. Against a champion with no dash, whose only escape is walking, that is the gap-closer, not a kiting tool. Flat 8s at every rank from 625 range.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard steals his Move Speed for 3s on a flat 8s cooldown from 625 range — it is how you get on top of an immobile Swain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (Q, cd 8, range 625, 'stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer carries no cooldown numbers at all, and the full layer gates every stage — including Level 2 — on 'Demonic Ascension's cooldown', an ability he does not have until 6.
audit.why: The punishable cooldowns are concrete: Nevermove 12s at rank 1, Vision of Empire 22s at rank 1, Demonic Ascension 120s against Unstoppable Force's 130s. Death's Hand is the opposite lesson and needs saying — at rank 5 it is a 3s cooldown, so waiting it out is never the plan.
audit.corrected: Commit inside the 12 seconds after Nevermove. Never plan around Death's Hand being down — it is 3s once maxed.

edits.before: Swain owns the first three levels here — you have no trade pattern and his E pull-into-root sets up a free W bomb plus Q poke that you simply can't answer at Level 1-2. Don't walk up to last-hit into his hook range; farm with Seismic Shard (Q) from max distance and let Granite Shield soak the chip whenever you back off. Respect the E root range above all — getting pulled in is how an early Swain snowballs this lane. Just survive and reach your stabilizing levels.
edits.after: Swain owns the first three levels — Death's Hand reaches 750 to Seismic Shard's 625 and you have no trade pattern that answers it. Nevermove is the ability to respect, and not the way most players think: the wave he throws out does not root, it roots on the way BACK to him. Step sideways after it has already passed you, not before it arrives. If it lands, the pull plus Vision of Empire and Death's Hand is free damage. Farm from max range, break off so Granite Shield recharges, and reach your spikes.

edits.before: This is where it turns. At Levels 4-5 Thunderclap (W) armor and Ground Slam (E) come online and Granite Shield lets you farm straight through his Q poke and W bomb chip without caring. Level 6 is your real spike: Unstoppable Force (R) is a hard knock-up that interrupts his channeled R drain mid-cast, so all-in him exactly when he commits his ultimate and the sustained fight he wants never happens. Bait the E hook with a Q-slowed dodge, then R-in for the kill window.
edits.after: This is where it turns. At Levels 4-5 Thunderclap (W) and Ground Slam (E) come online and Granite Shield lets you farm through his chip. Level 6 does not do what you have been told, though: Unstoppable Force will not interrupt Demonic Ascension, because that is a transform, not a channel — it runs as long as it keeps draining nearby champions, minions and monsters. Fight him off the wave, bring Grievous Wounds, and spend your 130s ultimate on his step-up in the 12s after Nevermove misses.

edits.before: You stay favoured into Swain late, and this is the rare AP lane where scaling helps YOU. Stack armor — Bramble Vest, Sunfire — and his AP drain barely chips your Granite Shield while your E and W keep growing off that armor. Just hold R for the moment he channels his Demonic Ascension drain in a teamfight: knocking him up cancels the drain and the soul stacks he lives on. Don't let him root-chain you in the open, but in a straight engage you win.
edits.after: You stay favoured into Swain, but for the right reason. His whole kit is magic, so armour defends nothing — Mercury's Treads and the Spirit Visage line are what make his poke harmless, while armour is an offensive buy here because Ground Slam's damage is calculated off it. Grievous Wounds is core: Ravenous Flock souls and the R drain are how he lives through a fight. Hold Unstoppable Force for his carry or his walk-up, and keep him off the minions the drain feeds on.

edits.after: Unstoppable Force at 6 gives you a 130s engage against his 120s ultimate — it displaces him and opens your burst, but it does not end the transform.

notes: Biggest fix: five strings claimed Unstoppable Force interrupts Demonic Ascension. It does not — Riot's own text calls it a transform whose form 'is indefinite', there is no channel flag on it, and acting on that line means spending a 130s ultimate for nothing. Second: the two layers disagreed on the build. Content told the player to stack armour against a champion whose every ability is magic; full already said 'Build MR (not armor)'. Armour is still correct to buy, but as an offensive stat, because Ground Slam's damage is computed from Malphite's Armor. NOT EDITED, NEEDS A HAND: the level chart. content win[] is ['Swain','Swain','Swain','Skill','Swain','Skill','Swain'] and the full layer's phases give Swain five of seven stages at 8.5/10 'Hard matchup', in a lane Malphite wins 54.15% over 591 games — and the entry's own whys[5]/whys[6] say Malphite out-trades from first item. win[4], win[5], win[6] should read 'Malphite' and the matching phases[4..6].side/.rating and diffRating should follow; these are enum-style values that cannot survive a +/-10% length band, so they are flagged here rather than proposed. TOOLING FLAG: _missing-interactions.json's 'resistances-invalidated — Swain bypasses stacking resistances (Ravenous Flock (P))' looks like a derivation artifact from the percentHealth flag. Ravenous Flock heals and grants permanent max health; it bypasses no resistance. The conclusion 'do not buy armour here' happens to be right, but for the unrelated reason that Swain is entirely magic damage, and I wrote it that way.
